_note: Narration script for the Chest pain module (CPP-007-AO v4.2). Lee on eleven_v4, one take, short conversational sentences (re-narrated 14 Oct 2026). Captions use the text here; the prompt starts with [calmly] and spells initialisms out (see tools/video/voice.json).

lines.head: Introduction
sentences: Chest pain.
What every Ambulance Officer needs to know.

lines.head: Think cardiac
sentences: Chest pain has lots of causes. But suspect cardiac ischaemia, unless there's an obvious alternative.
It can feel like pain, pressure, heaviness or tightness, in the chest, neck, jaw, arms, back or shoulder. Maybe with nausea, dizziness, sweating or shortness of breath.
Remember, time is muscle.

lines.head: First steps
sentences: Start with basic care, including ECG monitoring.
Check vital signs every 5 minutes, and consider clinical support.
And unless they're allergic, give oral aspirin, 300 milligrams.

lines.head: GTN limits
sentences: GTN is a sublingual dose of 300 micrograms. And it can drop the blood pressure.
So check first.
If they have GTN prescribed, the systolic needs to be at least 100. The pulse between 60 and 120. And no recent PDE-5 inhibitor.

lines.head: PDE-5 inhibitors
sentences: No GTN within 24 hours of sildenafil, vardenafil or avanafil. Or within 48 hours of tadalafil.
Together, they can cause life threatening low blood pressure.

lines.head: GTN prescribed
sentences: GTN prescribed, and the limits are met? Give one dose.
Then monitor vital signs every 3 to 5 minutes.
Pain still there, and the limits still hold? Repeat every 5 minutes as needed, up to a maximum of 3 doses.

lines.head: GTN not prescribed
sentences: No GTN prescribed? Consult the EOC Clinician. They may advise it.
The same limits apply. But the systolic must be above 100.

lines.head: Call the EOC
sentences: Consult the EOC Clinician if the blood pressure or heart rate falls outside the limits, at any time.
Or if the pain isn't resolved.
Or if pain that had gone away comes back.

lines.head: Checks and transport
sentences: Do the medication checks, with a second clinician whenever you can.
Then provide transport, and notify the receiving facility.

lines.head: Wrap-up
sentences: So. Think cardiac. Aspirin, unless they're allergic. Check pressure, pulse and PDE-5 before GTN. And stop at 3 doses.
Call the EOC Clinician if anything changes.
Now, have a go with the GTN checker on this page.
